sanskrit: grāmāgrahārakulyāḍhyo maṇihemajalārṇavaḥ jagat saṃplāvayām āsa dhṛtarāṣṭradayāmbudhiḥ
english: That ocean of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's compassion, rich with streams of villages and rent-free estates, its waters jewels and gold, flooded the whole world.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa putrapautrāṇāṃ pitṝṇām ātmanas tathā gāndhāryāś ca mahārāja pradadāv aurdhvadehikam
english: Thus, O great king, on behalf of his sons and grandsons, of his ancestors, of himself, and of Gāndhārī, he gave the funerary offerings for the departed.

sanskrit: pariśrānto yadāsīt sa dadad dānāny anekaśaḥ tato nirvartayām āsa dānayajñaṃ kurūdvahaḥ
english: When he had grown weary from bestowing gifts of every kind, the upholder of the Kurus brought his sacrifice of giving to its close.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa rājā kauravyaś cakre dānamahotsavam naṭanartakalāsyāḍhyaṃ bahvannarasadakṣiṇam
english: In this way the Kaurava king held a great festival of giving, abounding in actors, dancers and mimes, lavish with food, drink and priestly fees.

sanskrit: daśāham evaṃ dānāni dattvā rājāmbikāsutaḥ babhūva putrapautrāṇām anṛṇo bharatarṣabha
english: Having thus bestowed gifts for ten days, the king, the son of Ambikā, became free of debt to his sons and grandsons, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ prabhāte rājā sa dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ āhūya pāṇḍavān vīrān vanavāsakṛtakṣaṇaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then at daybreak King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the son of Ambikā, having fixed his hour for departing to the forest, summoned the heroic Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: gāndhārīsahito dhīmān abhinandya yathāvidhi kārttikyāṃ kārayitveṣṭiṃ brāhmaṇair vedapāragaiḥ
english: Wise, with Gāndhārī beside him, after greeting them in due form, on the full-moon day of Kārttika he had the sacrifice performed by Brāhmaṇas versed in the Vedas.

sanskrit: agnihotraṃ puraskṛtya valkalājinasaṃvṛtaḥ vadhūparivṛto rājā niryayau bhavanāt tataḥ
english: Setting the sacred fire before him, clad in bark and deerskin, surrounded by the women of his household, the king then went forth from the palace.

sanskrit: tataḥ striyaḥ kauravapāṇḍavānāṃ; yāś cāpy anyāḥ kauravarājavaṃśyāḥ tāsāṃ nādaḥ prādurāsīt tadānīṃ; vaicitravīrye nṛpatau prayāte
english: Then, as the king, the son of Vicitravīrya, set forth, a great wail arose from the women of the Kauravas and Pāṇḍavas, and from the other ladies of the royal house of the Kurus.

sanskrit: tato lājaiḥ sumanobhiś ca rājā; vicitrābhis tad gṛhaṃ pūjayitvā saṃyojyārthair bhṛtyajanaṃ ca sarvaṃ; tataḥ samutsṛjya yayau narendraḥ
english: Then the king, having honored that house with parched grain and many-hued flowers, and having provided for all his servants with wealth, dismissed them and departed.

sanskrit: tato rājā prāñjalir vepamāno; yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sasvanaṃ bāṣpakaṇṭhaḥ vilapyoccair hā mahārāja sādho; kva gantāsīty apatat tāta bhūmau
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, his palms joined and trembling, his throat choked with tears, cried aloud, 'Alas, great king, virtuous one, whither do you go, father!' and fell to the earth.

sanskrit: tathārjunas tīvraduḥkhābhitapto; muhur muhur niḥśvasan bhāratāgryaḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ maivam ity evam uktvā; nigṛhyāthodīdharat sīdamānaḥ
english: And Arjuna too, foremost of the Bharatas, scorched by keen grief, sighing again and again, said to Yudhiṣṭhira, 'Not so,' and grasping him as he sank, lifted him up.

sanskrit: vṛkodaraḥ phalgunaś caiva vīrau; mādrīputrau viduraḥ saṃjayaś ca vaiśyāputraḥ sahito gautamena; dhaumyo viprāś cānvayur bāṣpakaṇṭhāḥ
english: The heroes Vṛkodara and Phalguna, the two sons of Mādrī, Vidura and Saṃjaya, the son of the Vaiśya woman together with Gautama, Dhaumya and the Brāhmaṇas followed after, their throats choked with tears.

sanskrit: kuntī gāndhārīṃ baddhanetrāṃ vrajantīṃ; skandhāsaktaṃ hastam athodvahantī rājā gāndhāryāḥ skandhadeśe 'vasajya; pāṇiṃ yayau dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ pratītaḥ
english: Kuntī supported the hand of Gāndhārī, her eyes bound, as she walked, holding it laid upon her shoulder; and King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, resting his hand upon Gāndhārī's shoulder, went on serenely.

sanskrit: tathā kṛṣṇā draupadī yādavī ca; bālāpatyā cottarā kauravī ca citrāṅgadā yāś ca kāś cit striyo 'nyāḥ; sārdhaṃ rājñā prasthitās tā vadhūbhiḥ
english: So too Kṛṣṇā Draupadī and the Yādava lady, Uttarā of the Kurus with her infant child, Citrāṅgadā, and whatever other women there were—all set forth together with the king and his daughters-in-law.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ nādo rudatīnāṃ tadāsīd; rājan duḥkhāt kurarīṇām ivoccaiḥ tato niṣpetur brāhmaṇakṣatriyāṇāṃ; viṭśūdrāṇāṃ caiva nāryaḥ samantāt
english: The wail of those weeping women rose up loud then, O king, like the cry of ospreys in their grief; and from every side poured forth the women of the Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas, of the Vaiśyas and Śūdras as well.

sanskrit: tanniryāṇe duḥkhitaḥ pauravargo; gajāhvaye 'tīva babhūva rājan yathā pūrvaṃ gacchatāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ; dyūte rājan kauravāṇāṃ sabhāyām
english: At his going forth the townsfolk of Hāstinapura grieved exceedingly, O king, as they had once grieved before, when the Pāṇḍavas departed after the dice-game in the assembly hall of the Kurus.

sanskrit: yā nāpaśyac candramā naiva sūryo; rāmāḥ kadā cid api tasmin narendre mahāvanaṃ gacchati kauravendre; śokenārtā rājamārgaṃ prapeduḥ
english: Those women whom neither moon nor sun had ever beheld, now, when that lord of men, the chief of the Kurus, set out for the great forest, came forth into the royal highway, stricken with grief.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ prāsādaharmyeṣu vasudhāyāṃ ca pārthiva strīṇāṃ ca puruṣāṇāṃ ca sumahān nisvano 'bhavat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, O king, upon the palaces and mansions and upon the ground, there arose a very great clamor of women and of men.

sanskrit: sa rājā rājamārgeṇa nṛnārīsaṃkulena ca kathaṃ cin niryayau dhīmān vepamānaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: With difficulty the wise king made his way out along the royal road thronged with men and women, trembling, his palms joined in reverence.

sanskrit: sa vardhamānadvāreṇa niryayau gajasāhvayāt visarjayām āsa ca taṃ janaughaṃ sa muhur muhuḥ
english: He went out from Hāstinapura through the Vardhamāna gate, and again and again he bade the throng of people turn back.

sanskrit: vanaṃ gantuṃ ca viduro rājñā saha kṛtakṣaṇaḥ saṃjayaś ca mahāmātraḥ sūto gāvalgaṇis tathā
english: Vidura had resolved to go to the forest with the king, and so too had Saṃjaya the great minister, the charioteer, son of Gavalgaṇa.

sanskrit: kṛpaṃ nivartayām āsa yuyutsuṃ ca mahāratham dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpālaḥ paridāya yudhiṣṭhire
english: But King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the earth, sent back Kṛpa and the great warrior Yuyutsu, entrusting them to Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: nivṛtte pauravarge tu rājā sāntaḥpuras tadā dhṛtarāṣṭrābhyanujñāto nivartitum iyeṣa saḥ
english: When the townsfolk had turned back, the king with his retinue of women, that is Yudhiṣṭhira, granted leave by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, then wished himself to return.

sanskrit: so 'bravīn mātaraṃ kuntīm upetya bharatarṣabha ahaṃ rājānam anviṣye bhavatī vinivartatām
english: Approaching his mother Kuntī, O bull of the Bharatas, he said: 'I shall follow the king; let your ladyship turn back.'

sanskrit: vadhūparivṛtā rājñi nagaraṃ gantum arhasi rājā yātv eṣa dharmātmā tapase dhṛtaniścayaḥ
english: 'Surrounded by the daughters-in-law, O queen, you should return to the city. Let this righteous king go, firm in his resolve, to his austerities.'

sanskrit: ity uktā dharmarājena bāṣpavyākulalocanā jagādaivaṃ tadā kuntī gāndhārīṃ parigṛhya ha
english: Thus addressed by the King of Righteousness, her eyes troubled with tears, Kuntī then spoke in this way, clasping Gāndhārī to her.

sanskrit: sahadeve mahārāja mā pramādaṃ kṛthāḥ kva cit eṣa mām anurakto hi rājaṃs tvāṃ caiva nityadā
english: 'Toward Sahadeva, great king, never be neglectful in anything; for he, O king, is ever devoted to me and to you alike.'

sanskrit: karṇaṃ smarethāḥ satataṃ saṃgrāmeṣv apalāyinam avakīrṇo hi sa mayā vīro duṣprajñayā tadā
english: 'Remember Karṇa always, who never fled from battle; for that hero was cast off by me in my folly long ago.'

sanskrit: āyasaṃ hṛdayaṃ nūnaṃ mandāyā mama putraka yat sūryajam apaśyantyāḥ śatadhā na vidīryate
english: 'Surely, my child, the heart of your hapless mother is made of iron, since, not having looked upon the son of Sūrya, it does not shatter into a hundred pieces.'

sanskrit: evaṃgate tu kiṃ śakyaṃ mayā kartum ariṃdama mama doṣo 'yam atyarthaṃ khyāpito yan na sūryajaḥ tannimittaṃ mahābāho dānaṃ dadyās tvam uttamam
english: 'But things being thus, what could I do, O subduer of foes? Now this fault of mine, that I disowned the son of Sūrya, is openly known. On his account, mighty-armed one, you should give the highest gifts.'

sanskrit: sadaiva bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdham agrajasyārimardana draupadyāś ca priye nityaṃ sthātavyam arikarśana
english: 'Together with your brothers, O crusher of foes, you must always stand by the pleasure of your eldest brother and of Draupadī, O wearer-down of enemies.'

sanskrit: bhīmasenārjunau caiva nakulaś ca kurūdvaha samādheyās tvayā vīra tvayy adya kuladhūr gatā
english: 'Bhīmasena and Arjuna and Nakula, O upholder of the Kurus, must be kept in harmony by you, O hero; upon you now has fallen the burden of the family.'

sanskrit: śvaśrūśvaśurayoḥ pādāñ śuśrūṣantī vane tv aham gāndhārīsahitā vatsye tāpasī malapaṅkinī
english: 'But I, attending upon the feet of my mother-in-law and father-in-law in the forest, shall dwell together with Gāndhārī, an ascetic, soiled with dirt and mire.'

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa dharmātmā bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito vaśī viṣādam agamat tīvraṃ na ca kiṃ cid uvāca ha
english: Thus addressed, that righteous, self-controlled king, together with his brothers, fell into keen dejection and said nothing at all.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtam iva dhyātvā dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca mātaraṃ dīnaś cintāśokaparāyaṇaḥ
english: After reflecting for a moment, as it were, Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, wretched and given over to anxious grief, said to his mother:

sanskrit: kim idaṃ te vyavasitaṃ naivaṃ tvaṃ vaktum arhasi na tvām abhyanujānāmi prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
english: 'What is this you have resolved? You ought not to speak so. I do not grant you leave; you should be gracious to me.'

sanskrit: vyarocayaḥ purā hy asmān utsāhya priyadarśane vidurāyā vacobhis tvam asmān na tyaktum arhasi
english: 'Long ago, O you of lovely sight, urging us on, you stirred us up with the words of Vidurā; you ought not now to forsake us.'

sanskrit: nihatya pṛthivīpālān rājyaṃ prāptam idaṃ mayā tava prajñām upaśrutya vāsudevān nararṣabhāt
english: 'Having slain the kings of the earth, I won this kingdom, heeding your wisdom and that of Vāsudeva, the bull among men.'

sanskrit: kva sā buddhir iyaṃ cādya bhavatyā yā śrutā mayā kṣatradharme sthitiṃ hy uktvā tasyāś calitum icchasi
english: 'Where now is that counsel of yours which I once heard from you? For having taught me to stand firm in the Kṣatriya's duty, you now wish to swerve from it.'

sanskrit: asmān utsṛjya rājyaṃ ca snuṣāṃ cemāṃ yaśasvinīm kathaṃ vatsyasi śūnyeṣu vaneṣv amba prasīda me
english: 'Abandoning us, and the kingdom, and this illustrious daughter-in-law, how will you dwell in the desolate forests? Be gracious to me, mother.'

sanskrit: iti bāṣpakalāṃ vācaṃ kuntī putrasya śṛṇvatī jagāmaivāśrupūrṇākṣī bhīmas tām idam abravīt
english: Kuntī, hearing this tear-laden speech of her son, walked on still, her eyes brimming with tears; and Bhīma said this to her:

sanskrit: yadā rājyam idaṃ kunti bhoktavyaṃ putranirjitam prāptavyā rājadharmāś ca tadeyaṃ te kuto matiḥ
english: 'When this kingdom won by your sons is to be enjoyed, O Kuntī, and the duties of royalty are to be undertaken, whence comes this resolve of yours?'

sanskrit: kiṃ vayaṃ kāritāḥ pūrvaṃ bhavatyā pṛthivīkṣayam kasya hetoḥ parityajya vanaṃ gantum abhīpsasi
english: 'Why were we set by you long ago to bring about the destruction of the earth? For whose sake do you now wish to forsake us and go to the forest?'

sanskrit: vanāc cāpi kim ānītā bhavatyā bālakā vayam duḥkhaśokasamāviṣṭau mādrīputrāv imau tathā
english: 'Why, then, were we brought as children by you out of the forest, and these two sons of Mādrī as well, who are now overcome with sorrow and grief?'

sanskrit: prasīda mātar mā gās tvaṃ vanam adya yaśasvini śriyaṃ yaudhiṣṭhirīṃ tāvad bhuṅkṣva pārthabalārjitām
english: 'Be gracious, mother; do not go to the forest today, O illustrious one. Enjoy for a while the royal fortune of Yudhiṣṭhira, won by the might of Pārtha.'

sanskrit: iti sā niścitaivātha vanavāsakṛtakṣaṇā lālapyatāṃ bahuvidhaṃ putrāṇāṃ nākarod vacaḥ
english: But she, already resolved and with her hour fixed for forest-dwelling, paid no heed to the words of her sons, who lamented in many ways.

sanskrit: draupadī cānvayāc chvaśrūṃ viṣaṇṇavadanā tadā vanavāsāya gacchantīṃ rudatī bhadrayā saha
english: And Draupadī, her face downcast, weeping, followed after her mother-in-law as she set out for the forest, together with Bhadrā.

sanskrit: sā putrān rudataḥ sarvān muhur muhur avekṣatī jagāmaiva mahāprājñā vanāya kṛtaniścayā
english: That woman of great wisdom, looking again and again upon all her weeping sons, walked on still, firm in her resolve for the forest.

sanskrit: anvayuḥ pāṇḍavās tāṃ tu sabhṛtyāntaḥpurās tadā tataḥ pramṛjya sāśrūṇi putrān vacanam abravīt
english: The Pāṇḍavas, with their servants and the women of their household, followed after her then; and she, wiping away her tears, spoke these words to her sons:

sanskrit: kunty uvāca evam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi pāṇḍava kṛtam uddharṣaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ mayā vaḥ sīdatāṃ nṛpa
english: Kuntī said: It is even so, mighty-armed Pāṇḍava, as you say. In time past I roused you up when you were sinking, O king.

sanskrit: dyūtāpahṛtarājyānāṃ patitānāṃ sukhād api jñātibhiḥ paribhūtānāṃ kṛtam uddharṣaṇaṃ mayā
english: When your kingdom had been stolen by the dice-game, when you had fallen from happiness and were scorned by your kinsmen, then it was that I roused you up.

sanskrit: kathaṃ pāṇḍor na naśyeta saṃtatiḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ yaśaś ca vo na naśyeta iti coddharṣaṇaṃ kṛtam
english: 'How may the line of Pāṇḍu not perish, O bulls among men, and how may your fame not perish?'—it was for this that I roused you up.

sanskrit: yūyam indrasamāḥ sarve devatulyaparākramāḥ mā pareṣāṃ mukhaprekṣāḥ sthety evaṃ tat kṛtaṃ mayā
english: 'You are all the equals of Indra, godlike in your valor; do not stand gazing upon the faces of others'—thus was it done by me.

sanskrit: kathaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭho rājā tvaṃ vāsavopamaḥ punar vane na duḥkhī syā iti coddharṣaṇaṃ kṛtam
english: 'How may you, the best of the upholders of dharma, a king like Vāsava, not again be wretched in the forest?'—it was for this that I roused you up.

sanskrit: nāgāyutasamaprāṇaḥ khyātavikramapauruṣaḥ nāyaṃ bhīmo 'tyayaṃ gacched iti coddharṣaṇaṃ kṛtam
english: 'May this Bhīma, whose strength equals that of ten thousand elephants, of renowned might and manhood, not come to ruin'—it was for this that I roused you up.

sanskrit: bhīmasenād avarajas tathāyaṃ vāsavopamaḥ vijayo nāvasīdeta iti coddharṣaṇaṃ kṛtam
english: 'May this Vijaya, younger than Bhīmasena and like Vāsava, not sink down'—it was for this that I roused you up.

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca tathemau guruvartinau kṣudhā kathaṃ na sīdetām iti coddharṣaṇaṃ kṛtam
english: 'How may these two, Nakula and Sahadeva, obedient to their elders, not waste away from hunger?'—it was for this that I roused you up.

sanskrit: iyaṃ ca bṛhatī śyāmā śrīmaty āyatalocanā vṛthā sabhātale kliṣṭā mā bhūd iti ca tat kṛtam
english: 'And may this tall, dark, beautiful, large-eyed woman not be tormented in vain upon the floor of the assembly hall'—for this too was it done.

sanskrit: prekṣantyā me tadā hīmāṃ vepantīṃ kadalīm iva strīdharmiṇīm anindyāṅgīṃ tathā dyūtaparājitām
english: For I looked on then as she, trembling like a plantain-tree, in her courses, of faultless limbs, was thus lost at the dice-game—

sanskrit: duḥśāsano yadā mauḍhyād dāsīvat paryakarṣata tadaiva viditaṃ mahyaṃ parābhūtam idaṃ kulam
english: when Duḥśāsana in his folly dragged her about like a slave-girl, then it became known to me that this family was undone.

sanskrit: viṣaṇṇāḥ kuravaś caiva tadā me śvaśurādayaḥ yadaiṣā nātham icchantī vyalapat kurarī yathā
english: The Kurus too, my father-in-law and the rest, were stricken then, when she, seeking a protector, wailed like an osprey.

sanskrit: keśapakṣe parāmṛṣṭā pāpena hatabuddhinā yadā duḥśāsanenaiṣā tadā muhyāmy ahaṃ nṛpa
english: When she was seized by the hair by that wicked, witless Duḥśāsana, then, O king, I swooned away.

sanskrit: yuṣmattejovivṛddhyarthaṃ mayā hy uddharṣaṇaṃ kṛtam tadānīṃ vidurāvākyair iti tad vitta putrakāḥ
english: It was to increase your fiery valor that I roused you up at that time with the words of Vidurā; know this, my children.

sanskrit: kathaṃ na rājavaṃśo 'yaṃ naśyet prāpya sutān mama pāṇḍor iti mayā putra tasmād uddharṣaṇaṃ kṛtam
english: 'How may this royal line of Pāṇḍu, having obtained my sons, not perish?'—for this reason, my son, did I rouse you up.

sanskrit: na tasya putraḥ pautrau vā kuta eva sa pārthiva labhate sukṛtāṃl lokān yasmād vaṃśaḥ praṇaśyati
english: Neither his son nor his grandsons—how indeed should that man himself, O king, from whom a lineage perishes, attain the worlds won by good deeds?

sanskrit: bhuktaṃ rājyaphalaṃ putrā bhartur me vipulaṃ purā mahādānāni dattāni pītaḥ somo yathāvidhi
english: I have already enjoyed in full the fruit of my husband's kingdom long ago, my sons; great gifts were given, the Soma was drunk according to rule.

sanskrit: sāhaṃ nātmaphalārthaṃ vai vāsudevam acūcudam vidurāyāḥ pralāpais taiḥ plāvanārthaṃ tu tat kṛtam
english: It was not for my own gain that I urged on Vāsudeva; rather, with those speeches of Vidurā, it was done to wash away your dejection.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ rājyaphalaṃ putra kāmaye putranirjitam patilokān ahaṃ puṇyān kāmaye tapasā vibho
english: I do not desire the fruit of the kingdom won by my sons, my child; I desire, O lord, the holy worlds of my husband, through austerity.

sanskrit: śvaśrūśvaśurayoḥ kṛtvā śuśrūṣāṃ vanavāsinoḥ tapasā śoṣayiṣyāmi yudhiṣṭhira kalevaram
english: Doing service to my mother-in-law and father-in-law who dwell in the forest, I shall wither this body through austerity, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: nivartasva kuruśreṣṭha bhīmasenādibhiḥ saha dharme te dhīyatāṃ buddhir manas te mahad astu ca
english: Turn back, O best of the Kurus, with Bhīmasena and the rest. Let your mind be fixed upon dharma, and let your heart be great.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kuntyās tu vacanaṃ śrutvā pāṇḍavā rājasattama vrīḍitāḥ saṃnyavartanta pāñcālyā sahitānaghāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing the words of Kuntī, O best of kings, the sinless Pāṇḍavas turned back abashed, together with the Pāñcāla princess.

sanskrit: tataḥ śabdo mahān āsīt sarveṣām eva bhārata antaḥpurāṇāṃ rudatāṃ dṛṣṭvā kuntīṃ tathāgatām
english: Then there arose a great clamor from all the women of the inner apartments, O Bhārata, as they wept, seeing Kuntī come to such a pass.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇam athāvṛtya rājānaṃ pāṇḍavās tadā abhivādya nyavartanta pṛthāṃ tām anivartya vai
english: Then the Pāṇḍavas, having circled the king reverently and saluted him, turned back, without making Pṛthā turn back.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahārājo dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ gāndhārīṃ viduraṃ caiva samābhāṣya nigṛhya ca
english: Then the great king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Ambikā, addressing and restraining Gāndhārī and Vidura, spoke:

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasya jananī devī sādhu nivartyatām yathā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ prāha tat sarvaṃ satyam eva hi
english: 'Let the noble lady, the mother of Yudhiṣṭhira, be made to turn back properly; for all that Yudhiṣṭhira has said is indeed the truth.'

sanskrit: putraiśvaryaṃ mahad idam apāsya ca mahāphalam kā nu gacched vanaṃ durgaṃ putrān utsṛjya mūḍhavat
english: 'Casting aside this great and richly fruitful sovereignty of her sons, what woman would go to the impassable forest, abandoning her children, like one bereft of sense?'

sanskrit: rājyasthayā tapas taptaṃ dānaṃ dattaṃ vrataṃ kṛtam anayā śakyam adyeha śrūyatāṃ ca vaco mama
english: 'Remaining in the kingdom, she can practice austerity, give gifts, and keep vows even here today; let my words be heard.'

sanskrit: gāndhāri parituṣṭo 'smi vadhvāḥ śuśrūṣaṇena vai tasmāt tvam enāṃ dharmajñe samanujñātum arhasi
english: 'Gāndhārī, I am well pleased with the attendance of our daughter-in-law; therefore, O knower of dharma, you should grant her leave.'

sanskrit: ity uktā saubaleyī tu rājñā kuntīm uvāca ha tat sarvaṃ rājavacanaṃ svaṃ ca vākyaṃ viśeṣavat
english: Thus addressed by the king, the daughter of Subala spoke to Kuntī, repeating all the king's words and adding her own in particular.
